response.rationale: Folliculotropic mycosis fungoides is the most specific diagnosis, combining perifollicular infiltrates, follicular mucinosis, atypical lymphocytes, and clonal T-cell rearrangement. Mycosis fungoides (R1) is broader and lacks the follicular emphasis; other candidates are less specific or benign.

rejected.why: Too broad; folliculotropic variant is more precise given follicular involvement and mucin.
Pseudolymphoma is unlikely due to atypical lymphocytes and monoclonal T-cell rearrangement.
Follicular mucinosis is a histologic pattern, not a standalone diagnosis; here it is secondary to lymphoma.
